1. 제 2차 전도여행(고린도에서 안디옥까지): 1. The Second Missionary Journey (from Corinth to Antioch)
<행18:12~17> 갈리오가 아가야 총독 되었을 때에 유대인이 일제히:
<Acts 18:12~17> And when Gallio was the deputy of Achaia, the Jews made insurrection with one accord (people who rise up all together are usually the bad guys, right? A righteous man stands up alone.) against Paul, and brought him to the judgment seat, Saying, This fellow persuadeth men to worship God contrary to the law. And when Paul was now about to open his mouth, Gallio said unto the Jews, If it were a matter of wrong or wicked lewdness, O ye Jews, reason would that I should bear with you: But if it be a question of words and names, and of your law, look ye to it; for I will be no judge of such matters. And he drave them from the judgment seat. Then all the Greeks took Sosthenes, the chief ruler of the synagogue, and beat him before the judgment seat. And Gallio cared for none of those things.
 - This Gallio is the younger brother of Seneca, who was Emperor Nero's teacher.
 - When Gallio became governor of Achaia, the Jews thought, 'Let's finish this before he gets a grasp of the local situation,' and they all rose up together and accused Paul. So Paul is about to make his defense, but Gallio already gets it right away and throws them all out.
 - A very capable man. A man with good sense and judgment.
3차 전도여행(안디옥에서 에베소까지): The Third Missionary Journey (from Antioch to Ephesus)
<행18:18~23> 바울은 더 여러 날 유하다가 형제들을 작별하고 배: <Acts 18:18~23> And Paul after this tarried there yet a good while, and then took his leave of the brethren, and sailed thence into Syria, and with him Priscilla and Aquila; having shorn his head in ⑰ Cenchrea: for he had a vow. (So after finishing his year and a half of ministry in Corinth, he decided to go back to Syria, and it seems he had taken a Nazirite vow; he cut his hair in Cenchrea.) And he came to ⑱ Ephesus, and left them there: but he himself entered into the synagogue, and reasoned with the Jews. (He came to Ephesus, where he had wanted to go during the second missionary journey, and ministered there briefly; a little later you see him go back to Antioch and then travel around the regions of Galatia and Phrygia again, strengthening them. He probably went to check whether they were doing well after he had sent them Galatians.) When they desired him to tarry longer time with them, he consented not; But bade them farewell, saying, I will return again unto you, if God will. And he sailed from Ephesus. And when he had landed at ⑲ Caesarea, and gone up, and saluted ⑳ the church (Jerusalem), he went down to ㉑ Antioch.
2. 3차 전도여행(안디옥에서 에베소까지): 2. The Third Missionary Journey (from Antioch to Ephesus)
<행18:23>얼마 있다가 떠나 ①갈라디아와 브루기아 땅을 차례로 다니며:
<Acts 18:23> And after he had spent some time there, he departed, and went over all the country of ① Galatia and Phrygia in order, strengthening all the disciples.
 - From 'he departed' on is the third missionary journey.
 - At this time a man named Apollos, born in Alexandria, comes to Ephesus and works hard in ministry, and he's a real expert too. First of all, he knows the Scriptures thoroughly. And they say he was very eloquent - quite a contrast with Paul, right? Surprisingly, Paul was said to be a poor speaker. Anyway, he worked hard, but he didn't yet know much about Jesus and knew only the baptism of John.
그래서 브리스길라와 아굴라가 불러서 선은 이렇고 후는 이렇다 하면서 가르: So Priscilla and Aquila call him aside and teach him, "First it's this, then it's that," and since Apollos is so capable, he gets it right away, you know?
어디서 이런걸 배웠냐고: Where did you learn all this?
결국은 아볼로가 고린도로 건너가서 고린도 교회를 섬기게 됩니다. 그래서: In the end Apollos crosses over to Corinth and serves the Corinthian church. They say he was a great help there, but it doesn't seem to have done him much good personally. We'll look at 1 Corinthians in a bit, and Apollos really has a hard time there, you know? At the hands of the Corinthian believers. I've seen this kind of thing since I was a kid, so I know it well. Pastors go through all sorts of hardships. Sometimes they do a lot of good and still get driven out...
<행19:1> 아볼로가 고린도에 있을 때에 바울이 윗지방으로 다녀 ②에베:
<Acts 19:1> And it came to pass, that, while Apollos was at Corinth, Paul having passed through the upper coasts came to ② Ephesus: and finding certain disciples,
 - When Paul reaches Ephesus, he asks the people:
너희가 믿을 때에 성령을 받았는냐?: Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed?
We didn't even know there was such a thing.
그럼 너희가 무슨 세례를 받았는데?: Then what baptism did you receive?
그 요한이 세례줄 때 ‘내 뒤에 더 큰이가 오신다. 그 분을 믿어라 했는: When John baptized, he said, 'One greater than I is coming after me. Believe in Him,' and that One is Jesus. When he says that, the people are baptized in the name of Jesus. And then the Holy Spirit comes on them.
<행19:8~10> 바울이 회당에 들어가 석 달 동안을 담대히 하나님 나: <Acts 19:8~10> And he went into the synagogue, and spake boldly for the space of three months, disputing and persuading the things concerning the kingdom of God. But when divers were hardened, and believed not, but spake evil of that way before the multitude, he departed from them, and separated the disciples, disputing daily in the school of one Tyrannus. And this continued by the space of two years; so that all they which dwelt in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks.
바울이 예수의 이름으로 세례를 주니까 성령님이 임하셨는데 이 사건을 교두:
Paul baptized them in the name of Jesus and the Holy Spirit came, and using this event as a beachhead, he teaches about the kingdom of God for three months. It says some people were hardened, didn't obey, and got in the way - meaning even when the great Paul does it, even for three months, people with hard hearts won't listen. I've spread lectures like this many, many times too, and people who won't listen just won't listen.
 - So this time he simply borrowed the school of a man named Tyrannus and taught there separately for 2 years, and everyone in Asia heard the word of the Lord. When someone like Paul teaches for 2 years, things happen.
 - Because Paul did this, God did unusual miracles by Paul's hands: if they took handkerchiefs or aprons Paul had used and laid them on sick people, the sick were healed and evil spirits left. This is God proving that what Paul says is right.
이게 얼마나 신기했는지 어떤 마술사가 자기도 실험을 해 보는거예요. 이: This was so amazing that a certain magician tries it out himself. This magician calls a demon-possessed person and says, "I command you by the name of Jesus whom Paul preaches." Someone who doesn't believe says, "I command you in the name of Jesus," trying to copy it.
14절. 그런데 스게와라는 제사장이 아들이 일곱이 있는데 이걸 또 따라: Verse 14. And then there was a priest named Sceva who had seven sons, and they also tried copying this. Then the evil spirit says, "Jesus I know, and Paul I know; but who are ye?" and overpowers them, so you get this farce of them running away naked.
악귀가 아주 영악하죠? 마술사가 할 때는 가만히 있다가 제사장의 아들이:
The evil spirit is really cunning, isn't it? It stayed quiet when the magician did it, but when the priest's sons did it, it attacked them... Because of this, the Jews and Greeks living in Ephesus magnified the name of Jesus, people confessed their sins, and there was this work of God where they brought their books of magic and burned them up. The conclusion is that the word of God grew mightily and prevailed. It says the magic books they burned were worth fifty thousand pieces of silver, right? That's about 3.6 billion won.
  - At first Paul ministered for 3 weeks, a month, then the time gradually grew longer - three months, a year and a half in Corinth, and 3 years of ministry in Ephesus.
한 지역에서 사역하는 기간이 점점 길어지죠? 아마도 바울은 예수님이 금방:
The time he spends ministering in one area keeps getting longer, doesn't it? Paul apparently thought Jesus might come back any moment, so he was trying by any means to plant churches and preach the gospel in more places. But as time went on, it seems he realized Jesus' second coming wouldn't be as soon as he had thought. His thinking seems to have shifted toward, now I need to build up even one church properly.
 - During these 2~3 years of ministry in Ephesus, he writes 1 & 2 Corinthians.
All right, now let's go to 1 Corinthians.
